newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Jackson takes to stage in Seoul despite protests.
newsitem.headline: Jackson takes to stage in Seoul despite protests.

text.p: Pop superstar Michael Jackson shrugged off local outrage over his appearance in South Korea to dazzle thousands of screaming teenage girls on Friday at Seoul's 60,000-capacity Olympic Stadium.
But the performance failed to meet the lofty expectations of local promoters, who had predicted a sell-out. Only about 70 percent of tickets were sold, local media reported.

About 50 civic and religous groups had protested Jackson's visit, but South Korea's Ministry of Culture approved the current "HIStory World Tour" provided Jackson refrained from making "obscene or vulgar gestures or remarks".
Jackson, who will also perform in Seoul on Sunday, is scheduled to meet Cardinal Kim Sou-hwan, head of the Roman Catholic Church in South Korea, on Monday.
South Korea's main ticketing agencies at first refused to sell tickets to the peformances due to protests against the performance.
